coupling: The defect lives in the broken cross-commit invariant expectedSize == width*height*3. Commit 5eecd6a ('Limit AI7 thumbnail expansion') introduces ai7ThumbnailSize() to validate attacker-controlled AI7 thumbnail dimensions and cap the decoded RGB buffer at 256MB. The edited version still rejects width*height overflow and oversize results, but omits the overflow check on pixels*bytesPerPixel, so dimensions like 0x5555555555555556 x 1 make rgbSize wrap to 2, which passes the 256MB cap. On its own this is harmless: the existing decoder bounds every write by expectedSize itself (expectedSize - destPos >= num*3), so the wrapped size merely triggers a kerCorruptedMetadata error. Commit b7f1bd3 ('Improve performance of decodeAi7Thumbnail') rewrites the decoder to preallocate DataBuf(expectedSize) and, as part of the refactor, bounds the RLE write loop by a pixel budget numPixels = width*height passed in from the caller instead of by expectedSize. That bound is algebraically identical to the old one only when expectedSize == width*height*3 -- exactly the invariant the first edit silently broke. Composed, the decoder allocates a 2-byte heap buffer but accepts runs up to the unwrapped pixel count, so a single 255-pixel RLE run writes 765 bytes into it (ASan heap-buffer-overflow in decodeAi7Thumbnail). Neither diff contains the bug: each commit reviewed in isolation is correct, self-consistent maintenance (verified by execution: original batch clean, each single-edit tree clean, only the composed tree fires). A reviewer cannot locate the defect in any one commit's diff; fixing it requires recognizing that the second commit's new bound relies on a guarantee the first commit no longer provides, and restoring the invariant at either side of the commit pair.
